mainTopic: Preparation (זימון) of trapped fish and animals for יום טוב; slaughtering an endangered animal on יום טוב and רמי בר אבא's rule about flaying before eating
overview: This amud opens with the end of a ברייתא: a gift a נכרי brought from outside the תחום is forbidden to the Jew it was brought for, but permitted to a different Jew. Next comes רב's ruling that fish found in a water channel dammed on ערב יום טוב are permitted. רב חסדא (or רבה בר רב הונא) learns from this that a wild animal nesting in an orchard needs no זימון. רב נחמן rejects this, because damming was a real action and the orchard involved none. A ברייתא refutes the inference outright. Then a second ברייתא says the orchard animal needs no זימון. רב נחמן בר יצחק settles the contradiction: both speak of the young animal, and the difference is whether the garden is near the city or far from it. A new משנה follows about slaughtering an endangered animal on יום טוב and carrying meat home from the field. The גמרא then asks what רמי בר אבא's lesson about flaying and cutting before eating comes to teach. It shows that it cannot be rejecting רב הונא, and a new explanation begins that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A gift from outside the תחום: forbidden to its intended recipient, permitted to others
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes: something a נכרי brought from outside the תחום on יום טוב is אסור, but only to the Jew it was brought for. A different Jew may use it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it was brought from outside the תחום, it is forbidden. What was brought for this Jew is permitted to another Jew.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of a ברייתא, already underway on the previous amud, about gifts a נכרי brings to a Jew on יום טוב. It adds two final rules about items carried in from outside the תחום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An item carried from beyond the תחום is forbidden, so the Jew should not benefit from the נכרי's work done for him. The ban covers only the person it was brought for. Another Jew is fine, because nothing was done on his behalf.

keyTerms.meaning: Outside the boundary (about 2000 אמות) within which one may walk on שבת or יום טוב
Forbidden
Permitted
A different Jew

steps.confusionAlert: The item is not forbidden to everyone. The ban applies only to the Jew it was brought for.

phrases.english: From outside the boundary — it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: Continuation of the ברייתא about a נכרי's gift

phrases.english: And what came on behalf of this Jew —
is permitted to another Jew.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא from the previous section of the daf
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An item brought from outside the תחום is forbidden to the Jew it was brought for, but permitted to a different Jew.

steps.title: Fish found in a channel dammed before יום טוב are permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא quotes רב: if someone dammed a water channel on ערב יום טוב and found fish in it the next morning, the fish are permitted on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא said in the name of רב: One who dammed a water channel on ערב יום טוב, and the next day got up early and found fish in it, the fish are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic about trapping on יום טוב. It brings רב's ruling that fish found in a channel dammed before יום טוב may be eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By damming the channel before יום טוב, the person trapped the fish ahead of time. So they count as already caught and prepared before the holiday. No forbidden trapping happens on יום טוב itself.

keyTerms.meaning: One who dams or blocks up
A water channel, used for irrigation
The day before the holiday
He got up early
Fish
רבה, son of רב הונא

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling is the base text for the rest of this passage. Everyone that follows either learns from it or limits it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: הַסּוֹכֵר אַמַּת הַמַּיִם מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: One who dams a water channel on the eve of the Festival,

phrases.aramaic: וּלְמָחָר הִשְׁכִּים וּמָצָא בָּהּ דָּגִים — מוּתָּרִין.
phrases.english: and the next day rose early and found fish in it — they are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, trapping and preparation on יום טוב
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fish trapped in a channel dammed before יום טוב count as prepared and are permitted on יום טוב.

steps.title: רב חסדא learns that an animal nesting in an orchard needs no designation
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא draws a conclusion from רב's ruling: a wild animal that nested in an orchard needs no זימון (advance designation) before יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: From the words of our teacher (רב) we learn that a wild animal that nested in an orchard does not need designation.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא takes רב's fish ruling and applies it to a new case: a wild animal living in an orchard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא reasons that the fish were permitted because they were already confined and easy to reach before יום טוב. He thinks an animal nesting in an orchard is just as confined and reachable. So he concludes it counts as prepared even without anyone designating it.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, a student of רב
From the words of our teacher (here, רב)
We will learn
A wild (undomesticated) animal
That nested in an orchard
Designating something before יום טוב for use on the holiday

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said,
from the words of our teacher we learn:
an undomesticated animal that nested in an orchard —
does not require designation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a new rule from רב's fish ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב חסדא, a חיה nesting in an orchard needs no זימון, learned from רב's ruling about the fish.

steps.title: רב נחמן: our colleague has stumbled into a big matter
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rejects רב חסדא's conclusion. He says his colleague has 'fallen into a great matter,' meaning the comparison is mistaken.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: Our colleague has fallen into great things.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן pushes back on רב חסדא's conclusion. He says it does not follow from רב's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a sharp expression, רב נחמן signals that the conclusion about the orchard animal is a serious error. He does not explain why yet. Step 7 gives his reason.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, a colleague of רב חסדא and רב הונא
He fell
Our colleague
Into great or big matters, a figure of speech for a serious mistake

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
Our colleague has fallen into great matters.
phrases.notes: An idiom: he has made a weighty error

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference made in step 3
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the step from the fish case to the orchard animal. רב's ruling about the fish stays in place.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The two cases are not truly alike. This is explained in step 7.

steps.title: Another version: רבה בר רב הונא made the same inference
steps.stepSummary: A second version says it was רבה בר רב הונא, not רב חסדא, who learned from רב that an orchard animal needs no זימון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רבה בר רב הונא said, from the words of our teacher we learn that a wild animal that nested in an orchard does not need designation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another version of who made the inference. Here it is רבה בר רב הונא, the same person who quoted רב's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the speaker changes. The content of the inference is the same as in step 3. This version sets up a slightly different wording of רב נחמן's reply in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say, introducing another version of the story
Our teacher, meaning רב

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new law. It is the same claim as step 3, said in the name of a different person.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
Rabba bar Rav Huna said,
from the words of our teacher we learn:
an undomesticated animal that nested in an orchard —
does not require designation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the inference of step 3 under a different speaker
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this version, רבה בר רב הונא learns from רב that a חיה nesting in a פרדס needs no זימון.

steps.title: רב נחמן: the son of our colleague has stumbled
steps.stepSummary: In this version, רב נחמן says 'the son of our colleague has fallen into a great matter,' calling רבה the son of his colleague רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: The son of our colleague has fallen into great things.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives the same rejection. Since the speaker is now רבה, son of רב הונא, he calls him 'son of our colleague.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא was רב נחמן's colleague, so his son רבה is called 'בר חברין.' The rejection is the same as in step 4. Only the wording changes to match the speaker.

keyTerms.meaning: Son of
The son of our colleague
A leading student of רב and a colleague of רב נחמן

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
The son of our colleague has fallen into great matters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference in step 5, matching step 4
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only extending רב's ruling to the orchard animal
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The cases are not alike. This is explained in step 7.

steps.title: The difference: damming the channel was an action, the orchard involved none
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן explains: with the orchard animal, the person did nothing. With the fish, he did an action by damming the channel.
steps.simpleTranslation: There (the animal in the orchard), he did not do any action. Here (the dammed channel), he did an action.
steps.whatsHappening: This line gives the reason behind רב נחמן's rejection. It shows why the fish case cannot prove anything about the orchard animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fish count as prepared because the person actively trapped them before יום טוב by damming the channel. The animal wandered into the orchard on its own, and no one did anything to set it aside. So it still needs זימון.

keyTerms.meaning: There, the other case (the orchard animal)
Here, this case (the dammed channel)
He did not do
An action, a deliberate physical act

steps.whatToRemember: רב's ruling on the fish depends on the person's own action of damming before יום טוב. A wild animal that simply nested in an orchard, with no action taken, is not automatically prepared, and רב's ruling cannot prove that it is.
steps.confusionAlert: Watch the pointers: 'הָתָם' (there) means the orchard animal and 'הָכָא' (here) means the dammed channel, even though the channel was mentioned first.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a principle: an action taken before יום טוב (like damming) can make something count as prepared, while simply having it nearby does not.

phrases.english: There, he did not perform an action,
phrases.notes: The animal nesting in the orchard

phrases.english: here, he performed an action.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם לָא קָא עָבֵיד מַעֲשֶׂה, הָכָא קָא עָבֵיד מַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for רב נחמן's rejection in steps 4 and 6
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Separates רב's fish ruling from the orchard animal case. רב's ruling stays valid within its own case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The comparison ignores that damming the channel was an action taken before יום טוב, while the orchard animal involved no action at all.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Fish trapped by damming before יום טוב are permitted because of the person's action. An animal nesting in an orchard without any action is not proven to be exempt from זימון.

steps.title: רב נחמן proves from a ברייתא that the orchard animal needs designation
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן backs up his rejection by quoting a ברייתא that says an animal nesting in a פרדס does require זימון.
steps.simpleTranslation: And you say it does not need designation? But a ברייתא teaches: a wild animal that nested in an orchard needs designation. And a free bird needs its wings tied so it won't be mixed up with its mother. This is testimony given in the name of שמעיה and אבטליון.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן is finishing his attack on the conclusion drawn from רב. He brings an explicit ברייתא that says the opposite: the orchard animal DOES need זימון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Back in Step 7, רב נחמן gave a logical reason to reject the comparison to the fish. Now he adds a text: a ברייתא openly says חיה שקיננה בפרדס צריכה לזמן. Because it comes in the name of שמעיה and אבטליון, it carries great weight.

keyTerms.meaning: Designating something before יום טוב for use on יום טוב
'But isn't it taught in a ברייתא?' This opens a challenge from a ברייתא
An orchard. Here, an enclosed area where an animal is not fully trapped
A free bird, one that does not stay in a house
Early, very great sages, the teachers of הלל and שמאי

phrases.english: And does it not require designation?
But isn't it taught in a baraita:
A wild animal that nested in an orchard
requires designation,
and a free bird,
one must tie its wings
phrases.notes: Tying the wings acts as a sign marking this bird

phrases.english: so that it will not be mixed up with its mother.
And this is testimony that they testified
in the name of Shemaya and Avtalyon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a textual proof to רב נחמן's logical rejection in Step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion (of רב חסדא or רבה בר רב הונא) that an orchard animal needs no זימון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An explicit ברייתא states that an orchard animal requires זימון, which directly contradicts their conclusion

steps.title: The גמרא declares a decisive refutation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that the ברייתא decisively refutes the conclusion drawn from רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא announces that רב נחמן's challenge wins. The conclusion that an orchard animal needs no זימון has been knocked down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תיובתא means there is no answer, so the view is rejected. Only the conclusion drawn from רב falls. רב's own ruling about the fish still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A decisive refutation; the challenged view is rejected

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב himself was refuted. Only the students' comparison of the orchard animal to רב's fish case was rejected.

phrases.english: It is a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the challenge of Step 8 by accepting it
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The inference that an orchard animal needs no זימון is rejected

steps.title: A second ברייתא says the orchard animal needs no designation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר that says an orchard animal does NOT need זימון, which contradicts the first ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does it really need designation? But a ברייתא teaches in the name of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: בית שמאי and בית הלל agree that if someone designated birds inside the nest and found them in front of the nest, they are forbidden. When is this said? With dovecote doves, loft doves, and birds nesting in jars or in a building. But geese, chickens, house doves, and a wild animal that nested in an orchard are permitted and need no designation. A free bird needs its wings tied so it won't be mixed up with its mother. Birds that were tied or shaken as a sign are permitted in pits, houses, trenches, and caves. In trees they are forbidden, because one might climb and pick something. Birds tied or shaken by someone else are forbidden everywhere, because that would be stealing.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא raises a new problem. Another ברייתא openly says the orchard animal does NOT need זימון, so the two ברייתות seem to contradict each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא (Step 8) said חיה שקיננה בפרדס צריכה לזמן. This ברייתא lists the same animal among those that are מותרין ואין צריכין זימון. Both ברייתות agree about the free bird, which makes the disagreement about the orchard animal stand out even more.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And does it really need?' This questions what was just said
A תנא, the author of this ברייתא
A dovecote; its doves fly in and out freely
Birds that were shaken or handled as a way of designating them
Stealing. Tying or shaking a bird acquires it, so others may not take it

steps.confusionAlert: The last part of the ברייתא (tied or shaken birds, trees, stealing) is not the main point here. The key line is that חיה שקיננה בפרדס is listed as needing no זימון.

phrases.english: And does it really require designation?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: But isn't it taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said:
Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel agree
about birds that one designated inside the nest
and found them in front of the nest, that they are forbidden.
phrases.notes: They may be different birds that came from somewhere else

phrases.english: In what case is this said?
With dovecote doves and loft doves,
and birds that nested in jars or in a building.
But geese and chickens
and Herodian (domestic) doves
and a wild animal that nested in an orchard
are permitted, and do not require designation.
And a free bird needs its wings tied,
so that it will not be mixed up with its mother.
And those tied and those shaken (as a sign),
in pits, houses, trenches, or caves, are permitted,
but in trees, they are forbidden,
lest he climb up and detach something.
And those tied and those shaken (by someone else)
are forbidden everywhere, because of stealing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי בָּעֲיָא זִמּוּן? וְהָתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the ברייתא used in Steps 8 and 9 against a contradicting ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא of Step 8, which requires זימון for an orchard animal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's ברייתא explicitly lists the orchard animal as needing no זימון, so the two ברייתות contradict each other

steps.title: רב נחמן: one ברייתא is about the young animal, the other about its mother
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן settles the contradiction. The young animal needs no זימון, but its mother does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: There is no difficulty. This ברייתא is about the young animal, and that ברייתא is about its mother.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers the contradiction between the two ברייתות by saying they are talking about two different animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The young animal cannot escape the orchard, so it is already as good as caught and needs no זימון. The mother is bigger and can run away, so the ברייתא that requires זימון is talking about her. This way both ברייתות are correct.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is not difficult.' This introduces an answer to a contradiction
'This is about it (the young one), that is about its mother'

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: It is not difficult:
This one is about it (the young), that one is about its mother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: different animals (young versus mother)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seemed to speak about the same orchard animal and to contradict each other
steps.terutzMaskana: The young animal, which cannot escape, needs no זימון. The mother, which can escape, needs זימון.

steps.title: Is designation enough for the mother? She needs real trapping
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן's answer. If the mother can escape, זימון should not be enough; she should need a full trapping.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is designation enough for its mother? She needs a proper trapping!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב נחמן's answer. If the mother is free enough to run away, how can simply designating her be enough?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן said the mother needs זימון. But an animal that can escape is not yet trapped, and trapping it on יום טוב would be forbidden צידה. So זימון alone should not work for her; she should need a full trapping before יום טוב. The answer comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is it enough for her?'
A full, proper trapping, so the animal truly cannot escape

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the basic rule behind the whole סוגיא: זימון only helps an animal that is already effectively caught. It cannot replace actually trapping a free animal.

phrases.english: Is designation enough for its mother?
She requires a proper trapping!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in Step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that the mother is the case that needs זימון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An animal that can escape is not trapped, so designating it is not enough. It should need full צידה, so the ברייתא cannot be speaking about the mother.

steps.title: Both teachings refer to the young animal: a nearby garden versus a distant garden
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק sets aside the earlier answer. He explains that both ברייתות are talking about the young animal. One speaks of a garden near the city, and the other of a garden far from the city.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Both ברייתות are speaking about the young animal. The one that says no זימון is needed is about a garden near the city. The one that requires זימון is about a garden that is not near the city.
steps.whatsHappening: Since רב נחמן's answer about the mother ran into trouble, the גמרא gives a brand-new way to settle the two ברייתות. Both are about the young animal, and location makes the difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answer split the ברייתות between the young animal and its mother. That failed, because a mother who can escape would need real trapping, and זימון would not be enough. Now both cases involve the same young animal. If the garden is near the city, the animal is easy to reach and already counts as ready, so no זימון is needed. If the garden is far away, a זימון is required.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals that the earlier answer is dropped.
Both this one and that one
About it, meaning the young animal itself
A garden close to the city

steps.whatToRemember: Final answer: both ברייתות are about the young animal. Near the city, no זימון is needed. Far from the city, זימון is needed.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב נחמן בר יצחק is the same person as רב נחמן from the earlier steps. The word אלא shows he is replacing רב נחמן's answer about the mother.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Both this one and that one are about it (the young animal).
phrases.notes: Both ברייתות speak of the young animal that cannot escape.

phrases.english: This one is about a garden near the city,
phrases.notes: No זימון is needed. The animal is easy to reach and counts as ready.

phrases.english: That one is about a garden that is not near.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב נחמן's answer about the mother, which step 12 had challenged
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתות split between the young animal and its mother
steps.terutzMaskana: Both are about the young animal. The difference is whether the garden is near the city or far from it.

steps.title: Slaughtering an animal in danger of dying on a festival
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that an animal in danger of dying may be slaughtered on יום טוב only if there is still time to eat a כזית of roasted meat from it. רבי עקיבא says it is enough to have time to eat a raw כזית from the neck area.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If an animal is in danger of dying, one may not slaughter it on יום טוב unless there is still time in the day to eat a כזית of roasted meat from it. רבי עקיבא says: even enough time to eat a raw כזית from the place where it was slaughtered is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It asks when a person may slaughter a dying animal on יום טוב, mostly to save it from becoming a loss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slaughtering on יום טוב is allowed for festival food, so there must be a real chance to eat from the animal that day. The תנא קמא requires enough time to skin it, roast it, and eat a כזית. רבי עקיבא lowers the bar to eating a raw כזית straight from the neck, so less time is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal in danger of dying
Enough time left in the day
An olive-sized piece of roasted meat
From the place where it was slaughtered (the neck)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that permission to slaughter on יום טוב depends on a real chance of eating from the animal on the festival itself.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: An animal in danger of dying —
he may not slaughter it,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן יֵשׁ שְׁהוּת בַּיּוֹם
phrases.english: unless there is enough time in the day
to eat from it an olive-bulk of roasted meat.
Rabbi Akiva says:
Even an olive-bulk of raw meat from the place of its slaughter.
phrases.notes: No need for time to skin and roast it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה, unrelated to the זימון discussion
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dying animal may be slaughtered on יום טוב only if there is time to eat a roasted כזית. רבי עקיבא says time for a raw כזית is enough.

steps.title: Carrying meat home from the field by hand, limb by limb
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues: if someone slaughtered an animal in the field on יום טוב, he may not carry it on a pole. He must bring it home by hand, piece by piece.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he slaughtered it in the field, he may not bring it home on a pole or on a set of poles. But he may bring it in his hand, limb by limb.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a second rule about how to bring home meat that was slaughtered in the field on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying with a pole, or with poles shared by two people, looks like ordinary weekday hauling. To keep the festival feeling, he must change his normal way and carry the meat by hand in pieces.

keyTerms.meaning: A pole, or a set of poles carried by two people
Limb by limb, piece by piece

phrases.english: If he slaughtered it in the field —
he may not bring it on a pole or on a set of poles,
but he brings it in his hand, limb by limb.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁחָטָהּ בַּשָּׂדֶה לֹא יְבִיאֶנָּה בְּמוֹט וּבְמוֹטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second rule of the same משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Meat slaughtered in the field on יום טוב is carried home by hand in pieces, not on poles.

steps.title: Flaying and cutting before eating: proper manners learned from the burnt-offering
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר אבא teaches that the Torah's command to flay and cut up the עולה also applies to butchers. From this the Torah teaches proper manners: do not eat meat before it is flayed and cut.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רמי בר אבא said: Flaying and cutting are said about the עולה, and the same applies to butchers. From here the Torah taught proper manners: a person should not eat meat before it has been flayed and cut into pieces.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה with a teaching from רמי בר אבא about the normal order of preparing meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah tells the כהן to skin the עולה and cut it into pieces. רמי בר אבא applies this to ordinary butchers as a lesson in דרך ארץ, meaning proper manners. This background helps explain why רבי עקיבא's allowance of a raw כזית straight from the neck is unusual.

keyTerms.meaning: Flaying the hide and cutting the animal into pieces
Burnt-offering
Butchers
Proper manners or etiquette

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the Torah teaches proper conduct, and not only strict law, through the details of the קרבנות.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rami bar Abba said:
Flaying and cutting are stated regarding the burnt-offering,
and the same is true for butchers.
From here the Torah taught proper etiquette:
that a person should not eat meat
before flaying and cutting.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר אַבָּא הֶפְשֵׁט וְנִתּוּחַ בְּעוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה and relates to רבי עקיבא's raw-meat ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Meat should be flayed and cut before it is eaten, learned from the עולה as a lesson in proper manners.

steps.title: What is רמי בר אבא adding?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what new law רמי בר אבא is teaching. It suggests he means to reject the view of רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us? Should we say he comes to exclude the view of רב הונא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what point רמי בר אבא is making. It offers a first guess: he is coming to argue with רב הונא. This line sets up the next step, where רב הונא's view is quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רמי בר אבא said not to eat meat before it is flayed and cut up. One could read this as a demand to check the animal before eating it. That would clash with רב הונא, who holds a slaughtered animal is presumed fine without checking.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? What is new here?
If you say / Should we suggest
To exclude, to rule out a different view

phrases.english: (To exclude) What is he teaching us?
phrases.notes: The bracketed word לאפוקי is a marked textual variant. It is probably an extra word in the printed text.

phrases.english: If you say: to exclude the view of Rav Huna,

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן? אִילֵּימָא לְאַפּוֹקֵי מִדְּרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what point the teaching of רמי בר אבא from Step 16 is making.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new law רמי בר אבא is teaching. The first suggestion is that he rejects רב הונא's presumption.

steps.title: רב הונא's rule on the status of an animal before and after slaughter
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא teaches two rules. A living animal is presumed forbidden until we know it was slaughtered properly. Once it is slaughtered, it is presumed permitted until we know it became a טריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: An animal while alive stays in its forbidden status until you know how it was slaughtered. Once slaughtered, it stays in its permitted status until you know how it became a טריפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רב הונא's rule, which רמי בר אבא might be arguing with. There are two parts: before slaughter and after slaughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before שחיטה, the animal's starting status is forbidden. We need to know that a proper שחיטה took place. After a proper שחיטה, its starting status flips to permitted, so we do not need to search for a טריפה defect unless we actually know of one.

keyTerms.meaning: A presumed forbidden status
A presumed permitted status
It was ritually slaughtered
It became a טריפה, an animal with a fatal defect that is forbidden to eat

steps.confusionAlert: The two halves point in opposite directions. Before slaughter, the default is forbidden. After slaughter, the default is permitted. Do not mix them up.
steps.whyThisMatters: This presumption is why, in practice, a slaughtered animal does not need a full search for every possible defect.

phrases.english: As Rav Huna said:
An animal while it is alive —
stands in a presumption of being forbidden,
until it becomes known to you how it was slaughtered.
Once it was slaughtered, it stands in a presumption of being permitted,
until it becomes known to you how it became a tereifa.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא: בְּהֵמָה בְּחַיֶּיהָ בְּחֶזְקַת אִיסּוּר עוֹמֶדֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the view of רב הונא that Step 17 suggested רמי בר אבא is rejecting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A living animal is presumed forbidden until we know it was properly slaughtered. A slaughtered animal is presumed permitted until we know it is a טריפה.

steps.title: The משנה already seems to follow רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that our משנה already agrees with רב הונא. רבי עקיבא allows eating a raw כזית right from the place of slaughter, with no flaying or checking.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned our משנה in line with רב הונא! רבי עקיבא says: even a raw כזית from its 'בית טביחה'. Does that not mean the actual place of slaughter, the neck?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that רמי בר אבא argues with רב הונא. It points out that the משנה itself seems to support רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא said it is enough to have time to eat a raw כזית from the neck. That means eating right away, without flaying the hide or checking for defects, which fits רב הונא's presumption. So how could רמי בר אבא disagree with a view the משנה already supports?

keyTerms.meaning: But we have learned (in a משנה)! An opening for a challenge from a source
Its place of slaughter. The phrase whose meaning is being debated
Is it not that…? It pushes a proposed reading
Literally, actually

phrases.english: But we learned our Mishnah in accordance with Rav Huna!
As we learned: Rabbi Akiva says:
Even an olive-bulk of raw meat from its place of slaughter.
Is it not literally from its actual place of slaughter?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the suggestion from Step 17 by using the משנה from Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רמי בר אבא comes to reject רב הונא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי עקיבא allows eating raw meat from the neck right away, without flaying or checking. That supports רב הונא, so רמי בר אבא could not be arguing against him.

steps.title: בית טביחתה may mean the intestines
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. בית טביחתה can mean the place where the animal 'slaughters' its food, meaning the intestines. If so, flaying and checking are still needed first.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It means the place where the animal 'slaughters' (grinds) its food, the digestive organs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the reading from Step 19. It offers a different meaning of רבי עקיבא's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If בית טביחתה means the intestines, you cannot reach that meat without opening the animal. That means flaying it, and with that you can check it. So the משנה does not prove that one may eat without checking, and it gives no clear support to רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: No. It rejects the previous reading
'Slaughters' (grinds up) its food. A description of the digestive organs

steps.confusionAlert: Here the word טביחה does not mean שחיטה with a knife. It describes how the animal's insides break down its food.

phrases.english: No: from the place where it 'slaughters' its food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading of the משנה that Step 19 used to support רב הונא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the משנה is rejected. רב הונא's rule itself is not rejected.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The challenge assumed that בית טביחתה means the neck. It can instead mean the intestines, which require opening and checking the animal first.

steps.title: רבי חייא's teaching says the literal place of slaughter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the reading of בית טביחתה as the intestines. רבי חייא taught it means the actual place where the animal is slaughtered, the neck.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי חייא teach: 'The actual place of its slaughter'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against the answer it just gave. A ברייתא from רבי חייא clearly says 'the actual place of slaughter,' not the intestines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 20 the גמרא said בית טביחתה might mean the intestines, so flaying and checking would still be needed first. רבי חייא's word מַמָּשׁ ('actual') shows it means the real spot of slaughter, the neck. So רבי עקיבא really does allow eating from the neck without flaying or checking, and the משנה supports רב הונא after all.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't [he] teach? A formula that brings a ברייתא to challenge what was just said
A great collector of ברייתות; his teachings carry strong authority
The place of its slaughter, the neck where the cut is made
Actual, literally. It blocks any other reading

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two phrases. The משנה says בית טביחתה, which could be read two ways. רבי חייא says מקום טביחתה ממש, which can only mean the neck. That one extra word ממש settles it.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Chiya teach:
phrases.notes: Brings a ברייתא to challenge the previous דחיה

phrases.english: From the actual place of its slaughter?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the דחיה of step 20, bringing back the קשיא of step 19
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of בית טביחתה as the intestines (step 20)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי חייא's ברייתא says 'the actual place of slaughter.' That can only be the neck, so the intestines reading fails.
steps.whyThisMatters: Once this reading stands, the משנה clearly agrees with רב הונא. Then the suggestion that רמי בר אבא is rejecting רב הונא no longer works.

steps.title: A new explanation of רמי בר אבא begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops its earlier suggestion about רמי בר אבא and begins a new explanation of what he teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רמי בר אבא...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא says 'rather' to drop its first explanation of רמי בר אבא, and the new explanation continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 17 the גמרא suggested רמי בר אבא was rejecting רב הונא. Steps 19 to 21 showed the משנה agrees with רב הונא, so that suggestion cannot stand. The word אלא signals a fresh answer to step 17's question: what is רמי בר אבא teaching?

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. Signals the earlier suggestion is dropped and a new one is coming
The אמורא whose teaching about flaying and cutting meat is being explained

phrases.english: Rather, Rami bar Abba
phrases.notes: Opens a new explanation that continues on the next amud

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since step 21 showed the משנה supports רב הונא, the גמרא gives up the step 17 suggestion and begins a new one
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new law is רמי בר אבא teaching (step 17)?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not yet given. This line only opens the new answer, which follows on the next amud.
